Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: PII flow & log-retention — follow-up from demo

Hi Hannah / Rafael —

Thanks for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infra teams that we need clarified before procurement can move forward:

1) Network egress: we need a diagram that highlights all possible egress breakpoints for a Private/VPC deployment. Specifically: whether outbound traffic from model-serving nodes can be restricted to a set of customer-controlled NAT IPs (we prefer a single NAT address per region) and whether Redwood requires any outbound connections to third-party telemetry endpoints.

2) PII handling & retention: we need a clear table of what user content (request bodies, outputs, embeddings) Redwood persists by default in Private mode, and the retention windows and deletion controls available to customers. Our compliance team is looking for specific retention windows (e.g., 30d, 90d, 1y) and whether those are configurable per-tenant.

3) Logging/audit trails: list of logs generated (access logs, request metadata, request/response payloads, system-level telemetry) and which can be routed to our SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/HTTP ingest. Minimum retention requirement from our side is 3 years for audit trails. Can Redwood support exporting immutable logs to our S3 bucket or equivalent?

4) On-prem / air-gapped constraints: we are evaluating an air-gapped on-prem deployment for a subset of our workloads. What are the expected limitations (no outbound licensing calls, manual upgrades, key import/export via HSM)? Any redwood-managed control-plane dependencies we must be aware of?

If you can provide a short diagram and a retention matrix by end of day Thursday (6/2), that would be fantastic — procurement has an internal review next week.

Thanks,

Arielle Moss
Senior Security PM 
FinBoard, Inc.
arielle.moss@finboard.com

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -04:00

Hannah / Arielle — quick clarifications from infra/security after a run-through:

- Egress addressing: Our security policy prefers a predictable set of egress IPs per region; however, we need confirmation whether Redwood supports NAT gateway configuration that guarantees a stable outbound IP (or list of IPs) and whether any operations like license-checks or telemetry could break that model. If you require occasional outbound to redwood-managed endpoints, can those be whitelisted and are they negotiable for Private customers?

- Logging: We want to export immutable audit logs to our S3 bucket in addition to streaming to our SIEM. Retention for audit trails is 3 years minimum; for alerts/metrics we keep 1 year. Can logs be delivered as compressed JSON with SHA256 checksums (we ingest via S3 PUT events)?

- PII retention: For our regulated customers we need per-tenant configurable deletion (policy driven), and a documented deletion workflow (time-to-delete from request, whether backups are scrubbed). Also looking for confirmation that embeddings can be disabled from persistence for certain workloads.

- On-prem air-gap: two asks — a) does Redwood require an outbound TLS connection for license validation or crash reporting? b) do upgrades require build artifacts pulled from redwood-managed repositories or can they be delivered via offline media?

If you can confirm the above points and update the diagram/retention matrix to show where per-tenant toggles exist, we can greenlight the SOW.

-Jordan

Jordan / Arielle — thanks. Short answers here and next steps; Rafael and Ben will deliver the updated artifacts: 

1) Egress: Redwood Private supports customer-controlled NAT IPs and static egress via NAT Gateway or proxy. We do not require outbound telemetry endpoints for normal model serving. Any optional redwood-managed callbacks (usage reporting) are configurable and can be disabled for Private customers. Rafael will mark allowed/required outbound destinations in the updated diagram.

2) Log export & immutability: We can export audit logs to your S3 bucket (S3 PUT with server-side encryption). We can deliver logs as compressed JSON and include checksums (SHA256) on each file to support your ingestion pipeline. We will include a recommended retention model; by default Redwood retains request metadata for 90 days in Private mode unless configured longer.

3) PII retention: Per-tenant retention settings are supported in Private deployments; deletion workflows include immediate deletions for active stores and scheduled purges for backups (we document time-to-delete and will include steps to validate deletion). Embeddings persistence can be disabled on a per-workload basis; Rafael will include a checkbox in the matrix to indicate persistence toggles.

4) Air-gapped on-prem: No mandatory outbound TLS calls for license checks in the air-gapped package — upgrades are delivered as offline artifacts when requested. Some optional telemetry features will be unavailable in air-gap; Ben will enumerate manual maintenance steps in the playbook. HSM/KMS integrations are supported; we will document supported vendors and FIPS modes.

Action items & timeline:
- Rafael: Updated dataflow diagram with egress breakpoints + whitelistable endpoints (deliverable: redwood-private-vpc-dataflow-diagram-v3.pdf) — due Thu 7/2 EOD.
- Ben: Air-gap playbook + upgrade path + manual ops checklist (deliverable: rdw-airgap-playbook-v1.md) — due Thu 7/2 EOD.
- Monica: Share draft SOW language and procurement checklist (HubSpot deal updated).
- Hannah: Schedule deep-dive for Wed 7/8 10am ET; send calendar invite to FinBoard infra/security and Redwood SEs.
